body:
@farre WDYT about Q1 b?

Not applied yet: D1. Open: Q1.

New in this review:

D1: The new step branches on whether navigationParams's navigable is a top-level traversable, but [obtain a browsing context to use for a navigation response](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#obtain-browsing-context-navigation) branches on whether the navigable's active browsing context is a top-level browsing context. The two differ only for a traversable with a non-null parent, which doesn't exist today, so this isn't observable. If one existed, browsingContext could be in a new group while the agent comes from the outer page's group. Checking browsingContext itself doesn't work, because after a group switch its active document has no node navigable yet. Not applied: proposed fix is to make the condition "if navigationParams's navigable's active browsing context is a top-level browsing context".

Q1: shannonbooth [raised](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13034#discussion_r4198533591) giving every browsing context a group, set at creation and never changing, instead of looking up the top-level one here. Which way?

- a: Keep as is. Smallest change, and it's the same lookup as creating an auxiliary browsing context and, when fully active, as "create a new child navigable".
- b: Every browsing context gets a group at creation. Fixes this structurally and makes D1 moot. shannonbooth found it a bit less spec text overall, but it touches every place that reads a top-level browsing context's group and opens up other complexities. Not prototyped.
